item.title: How to Write a Better Business Proposal NEW — Wed Nov 4, 6:15 PM — Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - Classroom
item.description:
Are you beginning your entrepreneurial journey, seeking to improve your organizational fundraising, or maybe just looking to pressure test your proposal writing? Join this two session class to learn about turning your ideas into better stories. You’ll learn to identify key narrative elements from your work or idea, structure your writing the way a good story is structured, and how to use a marketing mindset to drive interest from potential investors or donors. Spread over two sessions, we’ll spend the first evening learning about best practices, and then have a class workshop on our second evening to have a healthy, learning, and productive session with class members’ actual proposals.
Gregor Clark is the Emmy-winning founder of Hiker, a creative agency based in Montclair. He has led (and sold) creative projects to hundreds of clients in his career, including Amazon, Chase, Verizon, and Facebook.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Washington DC 911 Trail Hike — Sun Nov 8, 8:30 AM
item.description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this second point to point hike of the weekend, this time covering the second of the two 911 Memorial Trail routes from DC into Maryland! After meeting, we'll shuttle with as few cars as possible, or maybe take the train, to our start point near the capital. We'll hike the Capital Mall, then head north along the trolley trail route, cut east through a grassy linear park, followed by Anacostia River Greenway to our end point! Distance will be about 15 miles and easy terrain. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374
Source: Meetup: Metrotrails Hiking

item.title: Critical Information Literacy and AI Literacy — Fri Nov 13, 11:00 AM — Online
item.description:
How can we help students become more discerning, critical, and responsible users of information in the age of AI? Join Bonnie Fong (Director, Bloomfield College Library) for an interactive professional development opportunity focused on Critical Information Literacy and AI Literacy. We will discuss effective ways we can teach students how to:
navigate and use information in an increasingly AI-driven information landscape, recognizing the limitations of AI tools and AI-generated content; critically evaluate information, identifying possible bias and reflecting on the existing economic, political, social, and cultural structures that impact information creation, dissemination, and access; and incorporate responsible and thoughtful AI practices into their academic work and possibly their life.

KPMG is a prominent global network of independent firms delivering professional audit, tax, and advisory services. As one of the prestigious "Big Four" accounting firms, it operates across roughly 140 countries and employs over 270,000 professionals worldwide. The organization was officially formed in 1987 through the merger of Peat Marwick International and Klynveld Main Goerdeler, with its name representing the initials of its foundational partners. Instead of functioning as a single multinational corporation, KPMG is structured as a network of distinct, locally managed member firms. Its primary client base includes major corporations, government agencies, and non-profit institutions seeking regulatory compliance and strategic business consulting. Through this decentralized model, the firm maintains a massive footprint in global financial compliance and corporate restructuring.
Hosted by: Accounting Society
